content:
emily: Quick report - a customer reported tokens being billed twice when a stream was truncated by the quota enforcer and the client retried with a fresh request_id. Looks like the replay path and truncation path both produced credits.

tonys: Can you paste the trace? streaming + toolcall or plain generate?

emily: Streaming with toolcalls. Flow: client stream -> quota enforced truncation returns partial EOF -> client retries with new request_id -> router routes to a replay node which replays same suffix -> both writes land in ledger. Snippet: 

```
[2026-03-22T11:23:10Z] session=abc stream_offset=12288 quota=enforce truncation_offset=12288 tokens=40 label=quota-enforce
[2026-03-22T11:23:10Z] ledger.write session=abc offset=12288 tokens=40 reason=quota_enforce counted=true write_id=wid-157
[2026-03-22T11:23:11Z] client retry new_request_id=req-999 route=replay resume_offset=12288 tokens=40
[2026-03-22T11:23:11Z] ledger.write session=abc offset=12288 tokens=40 reason=replay counted=true write_id=wid-158 <-- duplicate
```

tonys: Issue seems different from aggregator-window dups. Here request_id differs so write_id differs. We need a canonical dedupe key that survives retries with new request_id.

rachel: Idea: compute a dedupe signature at router time from (session_id, offset, canonical_prefix_hash, credit_reason). Use that as ingest key. If two writes share signature, drop the second or mark provisional flip.

emily: Canonical_prefix_hash depends on whether router normalizes metadata. For quota-triggered truncation, primary and replay might have different labels. Could prefix the hash with the original payload hash (if present) to make it more stable.

tonys: Payload hash requires router to stash original request digest. That adds overhead but is doable. Alternate: provisional credits with short TTL and auto-confirm on explicit ack. That matches other discussions but requires console work.

rachel: If we do provisional, console needs immediate visibility. Finance will want an aggregated column to exclude provisional credits by default. Add a `billing.view` query param to show provisional.

emily: Also need telemetry: emit `billing.dup_signature` metric and `billing.duplicate_detected` counter when signature collision occurs, plus `billing.provisional.ttl_expiry`.

tonys: Rollout: flag `billing.dedupe_signature_v1`. Start canary 2% traffic. Monitor `billing.duplicate_detected` drop and `billing.provisional.flip_rate`. If signature approach reduces duplicates to near zero, we can phase out provisional semantics.

rachel: Edgecase: if the client intentionally replays with modified payload (e.g., different toolcall args) but same offset, signature might collide incorrectly. We need to include a `request_fingerprint` that incorporates toolcall args. Otherwise we may under-credit.

emily: Good point. For safety, on signature collision, store both candidate writes with provenance and let the confirm path disambiguate. I prefer signature as a fast-path dedupe only; fallback to provisional flip when ambiguous.

dev-bot: [note] saved repro trace to /tmp/billing-repro-abc-3100009876.log

finance: Heads up - finance is sensitive to any visible provisional credits. Please coordinate before canary and send a short blurb explaining provisional semantics and TTL.

tonys: Action items: 1) implement signature generation at router (rachel) 2) ingest-side dedupe fast-path using signature (tony) 3) provisional fallback + TTL job (emily) 4) dashboard filter + finance blurb (rachel).

emily: I'll open INF-2026-788 with the repro and plan. Will attach quick perf numbers for signature hashing overhead.
rachel: I'll prototype a dashboard tile showing duplicates over time and a link to accounts with high provisional churn.
tonys: Let's gate behind `billing.dedupe_signature_v1` and run for 48h in canary. If stable, roll to 20% then 100%.
emily: Thanks. setting up PRs and will @-mention reviewers when ready. :thumbsup:
